title: Add quantization quality sanity suite (golden prompts + lightweight scoring)
author: Priyanka Bose
description: Motivation: During the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we’re moving quickly on kernel dispatch + quantization profile defaults. We need a fast “tripwire” to catch obvious quality regressions (e.g., broken JSON/tool call formatting, language drift, refusal spikes, or summarization truncation) before we flip defaults or broaden canary cohorts. This PR adds a lightweight quantization quality sanity suite built around a small set of golden prompts + deterministic decoding and cheap scoring. Scope: (1) Add `quant_sanity` runner that executes a fixed prompt set and compares against stored goldens, (2) Add scoring utilities focused on obvious failures (structure + similarity), (3) Provide CLI + CI wiring to run on PRs that touch quantization/kernels/profiles (opt-in label for now), and (4) Document update workflow for goldens (manual, reviewed). What this is / isn’t: This is not meant to replace the full benchmark suite v3 or Applied ML eval sign-off. It is intentionally small and cheap (minutes) and optimized for catching “something is clearly wrong” changes. Prompt set: 52 prompts (balanced) across summarization, extraction to JSON, tool-calling style responses, short QA, and long-context sanity (truncated to keep runtime low). The prompts are derived from existing internal prompt sets but reduced and scrubbed for CI; no customer data. Determinism + decoding: temperature=0, top_p=1, max_tokens fixed per case; seed pinned where supported; normalization handles whitespace + minor punctuation drift. Scoring: (a) JSON/schema parse success for structured cases, (b) key presence + type checks for extraction cases, (c) normalized edit distance / token overlap score for freeform cases (thresholded), (d) “refusal” and “empty output” heuristics, (e) length / truncation guardrails for summaries. Output + artifacts: runner writes a single JSONL results file + a summary table; on failure includes top diffs and the exact command line used. Goldens: stored in-repo under `eval_harness/goldens/quant_sanity/` with a `GOLDENS.md` explaining update procedure. Updates require `--update-goldens` and are blocked in CI (only allowed locally), intended to be reviewed by Applied ML (Jonas/Olivia) when thresholds move. Usage: `python -m eval_harness.quant_sanity --model <model_id> --mode {baseline|fp8|int8} --endpoint $REDWOOD_ENDPOINT --api-key $REDWOOD_API_KEY --out results.jsonl` and `python -m eval_harness.quant_sanity --compare results.jsonl --goldens eval_harness/goldens/quant_sanity/goldens.jsonl`. CI: Adds `quant-sanity-smoke` job that runs the compare step (no network) + validates the prompt set and scorer; optional GPU run is behind `run-gpu-evals` label for now (we can flip to required once runtime team is happy with capacity/noise). Notes: This was requested after SUP-31852 (INT8 quality concerns) and to support the runtime sprint’s faster iteration loop. It should also help interpret perf canary anomalies where output degradation shows up as “success” but customers report issues.

review_conversation: Jonas Weber: Can we make sure this doesn’t become a de-facto approval gate? Also, what’s the failure mode if a model legitimately changes phrasing but is still fine?

Priyanka Bose: Agreed. I added explicit language in README + workflow comments: this is a regression tripwire only. For phrasing drift we’re using tolerant similarity thresholds for freeform cases + hard structural checks only where we must. Also added a summary of which cases are “hard” vs “soft” scored.

Claire Dubois: Determinism worries me. Even with temp=0 we’ve seen small nondeterminism on GPU. Can we avoid flaky CI? Also: please pin max_tokens per test and ensure the scorer handles whitespace/newlines consistently.

Priyanka Bose: Updated: CI default job is compare-only + prompt/scorer validation (no model call). The GPU run is label-gated. Also pinned per-case max_tokens and added `normalize_text()` that collapses whitespace + normalizes common punctuation.
Arjun Desai: For INT8, common regressions are malformed JSON and numeric field drift. Can we add type checks and allow small numeric tolerance?

Priyanka Bose: Added schema/type checks for the extraction prompts and a numeric tolerance for known numeric fields (relative tolerance 2% unless overridden in the case metadata). Also added explicit counters for json_parse_fail / schema_fail so we can track improvements over time.
Olivia Grant: Can we add a refusal detector? We’ve had cases where quant changes increase refusals without tripping similarity metrics.
Priyanka Bose: Added refusal/empty-output heuristics (keyword + length + leading phrases) and made them hard-fail for the affected prompt subset. The summary now includes refusal_rate and empty_rate.
Rina Kobayashi: Please align naming with runtime sprint docs: we use “baseline/fp8/int8” consistently. Also, can this output a single-line summary that can be pasted into Slack triage threads?
Priyanka Bose: Renamed modes to baseline/fp8/int8. Added `--slack-summary` which prints a compact line: pass/fail + counts + worst offenders and a path to artifacts.
Jonas Weber: Final nit: goldens update should be noisy by design. Please make sure `--update-goldens` is blocked in CI and documented as “requires Applied ML review.”
Priyanka Bose: Done. CI refuses `--update-goldens` (explicit guard). GOLDENS.md now includes “reviewers: Applied ML/Evals” and a checklist.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Jonas Weber. Post-merge note: we’ll trial the label-gated GPU run during the sprint and decide whether to make it required once we’ve measured flake rate + capacity impact.
